source.title: Convolutions in geometric function theory: Recent results and open problems.

accepted.question_text: Let S be the class of analytic univalent functions on the unit disk D = {z : |z| < 1} that are normalized by g(z) = z + ⋯. For each direction ψ, let C_ψ be the subclass of S consisting of functions that are convex in the direction ψ. Define DCP to be the family of analytic functions f on the unit disk such that, for every ψ ∈ [-π, π] and every g ∈ C_ψ, the Hadamard convolution f * g belongs to C_ψ. Is the truncated exponential polynomial ∑_{k=0}^{n} (1+z)^k / k! contained in DCP for general n? The source notes that this has been verified for n ≤ 20.
accepted.context_brief: Hadamard convolution and the class DCP

evidence.quote: Let C_{\psi} denote the subset of functions f\in S=\{g: g(z)=z+..\). analytic univalent in D=\{| z| <1\}\} that are convex in the direction \psi. Then the class DCP is the family \{ f: f analytic in U, f*g\in C_{\psi} for all \psi\in [-\pi,\pi] and all g\in C_{\psi}\}.
He asks, for example, whether \sum^{n}_{k=0}(1+z)^ k/k!\in DCP\; this is true for n\leq 20.

accepted.question_text: Suppose f(z) = ∑_{k=1}^{∞} a_k z^k is subordinate to a function F(z) = ∑_{k=1}^{∞} b_k z^k, where both f and F are analytic on the unit disk and F is convex there. For which exponents p ≥ 2 does one always have the coefficient inequality ∑_{k=1}^{n} |a_k|^p ≤ ∑_{k=1}^{n} |b_k|^p? The source says this is known when p is an even integer and asks whether it remains true for a large set of exponents p ≥ 2.
accepted.context_brief: Coefficient inequalities under subordination to convex functions

evidence.quote: If f(z)=\sum^{\infty}_{1}a_ kz^ k\prec F(z)\leq \sum^{\infty}_{1}b_ kz^ k, where f, F are analytic and F convex in U, he asks whether \sum^{n}_{1}| a_ k|^ p\leq \sum^{n}_{1}| b_ k|^ p, for some large set of p\geq 2\; this is true if p is an even integer.

accepted.question_text: Let S be the class of normalized univalent analytic functions on the unit disk D. Let 𝒟 = {f : f(z) = z + a_2 z^2 + ⋯ on D and |f''(z)| ≤ Re f'(z)}. If g and h are normalized functions in S and f ∈ 𝒟, must the Hadamard triple convolution satisfy Re((f * g * h)(z)) > 0 for every z in D?

evidence.quote: Let {\mathcal D}=\{f: f(z)=z+a_ 2z^ 2+..\). in D, with | f''(z)| \leq Re f'(z)\}. He asks whether, for normalized functions g, h in S and a function f in {\mathcal D}, we have Re((f*g*h)(z))>0 in D.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Also the coefficient problem for {\mathcal D} is open.

evidence.quote: Also the coefficient problem for {\mathcal D} is open.

needs_review.question_text_raw: If V, W are compact, complete subsets of A_0 with du(V)=du(W), is it true that du(V\cap W)=du(V)?

evidence.quote: Let A_ 0=\{f: f(z)=1+..\). analytic in D\}, and for any subset V of A_ 0 let its dual set be V^*=\{g: g\in A_ 0, (f*g)(z)\neq 0 for any z in D and any f in V\} and its dual hull, such as: If V, W are compact, complete subsets of A_ 0 with du(V)=du(W), is it true that du(V\cap W)=du(V)?
